slides.title: IntegrationRescue
slides.message: The AI agent that fixes broken SaaS integrations and proves the business outcome.
slides.notes: Title card at the start of the presentation part. No narration needed.

slides.title: Paid. Still on Free.
slides.message: Every system reports success while the customer loses what they paid for.
slides.footer: No alert fires. Support escalates. An engineer traces it by hand across four systems.
slides.notes: What you just saw is a failure no dashboard catches. The customer paid, every system said success, and the customer still couldn't use what they paid for. Someone has to notice. Then an engineer spends hours tracing it across billing, webhooks, code and access data.

slides.title: Why today's tools stop short
slides.message: Each tool checks its own layer. Nobody checks the customer's outcome.
columns: Start from an alert; none fires
slides.footer: The gap: verifying the business outcome across systems
slides.small: Comparison with a general coding agent: protocol ready, not yet run. No superiority claim.
slides.notes: Today's tools stop early. Monitoring sees a 202 and is happy. Coding assistants can write a patch, but they judge success by tests passing, not by whether the customer actually got access.

slides.title: IntegrationRescue
slides.message: An AI agent that investigates like a careful engineer, and only claims what an independent check proves.
bullets: Live Gemini agent chooses every tool call and hypothesis
Smallest repair, tested in an isolated copy
A human approves; a read-only verifier proves
slides.notes: IntegrationRescue is an AI agent that works like a careful engineer. It forms hypotheses, checks each system, reproduces the failure in a copy and proposes the smallest fix.
slides.source: Screenshot: live Gemini run inc_2376f4f829 (13 model calls, VERIFIED); AGENT_CARD.md

slides.title: How the agent works
slides.message: The model decides. Deterministic code enforces.
left: Whether a fix is needed at all
slides.notes: It tests the fix and asks a human to approve. Then a separate verifier, which the AI cannot influence, checks the business result: right plan, one charge, one grant. That's why it's an agent and not an automation: it decides what to investigate, whether a fix is needed at all, and when it can't know.

slides.title: Live demo
slides.message: A real Gemini-powered run, end to end, in under two minutes.
slides.notes: The two-minute demo plays here (0:00-2:00 of the pitch video). It is a recording of a real Gemini-powered run; the investigation path is produced by the agent, not replayed from the baseline.

slides.title: Architecture
slides.message: One container: agent, policy layer, simulated systems, sandbox, verifier, dashboard.
slides.notes: Backup slide for Q&A; not narrated in the six-minute video. Gemini today; a Claude adapter exists (fake-client tested only); the deterministic baseline is for tests and comparison and is never presented as the AI.

slides.title: Reliability evidence
slides.message: Measured on live Gemini, including what does not work yet.
tiles: correct outcomes after the tool fix
slides.footnote: Live: gemini-3.1-flash-lite, free tier, 2 seeds per variant; 31 scored live runs, 72 recorded runs in total (live + baseline). Small samples.
slides.notes: We measure this. In live tests with Google Gemini, the agent diagnosed all 31 scored incidents correctly. After one fix to our tools, it reached the right outcome in 16 of 17, and all 11 configuration and trust repairs were verified. Zero false success claims, zero double charges. Code repairs are not reliable yet: zero of five. We publish that too.

slides.title: Safety and human oversight
slides.message: Safety lives in code, not in the prompt.
bullets: Every repair waits for a human
Only the read-only verifier can say VERIFIED
Live test: the AI trusted an unannounced signing key. Now blocked in code, whatever the model proposes
Model outage shows MODEL UNAVAILABLE, never success
slides.notes: Safety lives in code, not in the prompt. In one test, the AI trusted a security key it should have checked. We didn't just change the prompt. We made the system refuse that change, whatever the model says. Every repair needs human approval, and only the independent check can say verified.
slides.source: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md; test_delivery_families.py; test_provider_failures.py; screenshots from inc_2376f4f829

slides.title: Defensibility
slides.message: Verified outcomes on a growing library of incident patterns.
nodes: Test case with hidden ground truth
slides.small: Today: 5 incident families, simulated. The library grows only with real pilots.
slides.notes: Our advantage is verified outcomes. Every incident becomes a test case with hidden ground truth, so we can prove reliability, and that library grows with every pilot. And we're model-agnostic.

slides.title: Business model
slides.message: Pay for proven fixes, not attempts.
slides.segment: Beachhead (hypothesis): B2B SaaS, roughly 20–300 staff, billing on Stripe / Chargebee / Paddle controls product access
slides.measured: Measured: 11–18 model calls, 35k–70k input tokens per incident (live means, free tier)
slides.notes: We plan to charge for outcomes: a platform fee, plus a fee per verified fix, and nothing for a guess. Fallback: That pricing is a hypothesis we'll test with design partners.
